raw_response:
I will keep most of my land in the wheat-maize rotation because that is the most reliable way for me to get grain from my 5 mu, and I have well irrigation to support it. Since some family labor is away from home, I will not put too much land into labor-heavy cotton. I will keep a smaller cotton area just to maintain cash income, and I will plant some peanut because it fits my land and spreads risk. For wheat, I will use improved seed, apply moderate fertilizer, irrigate a few times, and aim for a steady yield rather than pushing too hard. After wheat harvest, I will plant hybrid summer maize on the same land because it gives stable production and uses the season well. For peanut, I will manage fertilizer more carefully and keep irrigation moderate because it does not need as much water as wheat. For cotton, I will keep inputs controlled, use improved seed, and spray more times than the other crops because pest pressure is usually higher. I will use rotary tillage on most plots because it saves labor and works for my small farm. Overall, I am choosing a steady, practical plan that balances grain for security, some cash crops for income, and labor that my household can actually handle.
